name: Lemaître’s expansion and nebular velocities
description: Lemaître related a nonstatic relativistic cosmological model to available nebular distances and radial velocities.

impact.note: Provisional consequence judgement; actual reach and later attribution require independent study.

date.basis: The cited evidence dates this scoped historical episode; no global priority is implied.

events.statement: Lemaître published an expanding-universe model and a velocity–distance relationship.

evidence.supports: Relates Lemaître’s nonstatic model to distances and velocities and reports both historical coefficients.

contributions.resource: Developed the model and connected it to astronomical observations.

evidence.supports: Relates Lemaître’s nonstatic model to distances and velocities and reports both historical coefficients.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode supported by the evidence collected here; not a global-priority claim.

caveats: Historical estimates depend on grouping and distance calibration; Slipher supplied many velocities via Strömberg. Hubble’s 1929 analysis is distinct. Whether Lemaître knew Friedmann’s 1922 work is not established here.

research.note: Independent source reading checked dated events, linked theory and numerical measures. Grain, impact and other unreviewed facets remain provisional.
